detail.body:
## What

The block-sparse QSA suites of the gated attention block -- `test_block_qsa_end_to_end.py` and `test_block_qsa_decode.py` -- held the **gated O** against the fp32 oracle at an absolute `atol 2e-2`. That number is the SDPA stage test's bar on the **LSE** (`test_sdpa_stage_sm107.py`; its O checks are `cos > 0.999`), transplanted onto bf16 O values of magnitude up to ~3, where one bf16 ulp is 0.015625 (78 % of the bar) and any single rounding flip at `|O| >= 4` (ulp 0.03125) would exceed it for every implementation alike.

This PR makes the gate the repo's **existing bf16 / f16 output convention** -- the one the block backward suite calibrated once on Rubin and never widened (`test_block_backward.py`): per element

```
|d| <= 2^-7 * max|ref| + 2^-6 * |ref|      and      cos >= 0.999        (bf16; f16: 2^-10 / 2^-9)
```

* New shared helper `test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/gated_block_bounds.py` (`assert_output_close`, `output_bound_stats`, the three constants). `test_block_backward.py` now imports its constants from it, so the numbers have ONE definition.
* The two QSA suites use `assert_output_close` on every gated-O comparison against the oracle (the dense `_check`, the packed per-sequence `_check_thd`, the decode `_Case.check`, the MTP pos0 reading, the adversarial cell's rows below the identity bound) and on the kernel-vs-kernel comparisons (fused vs unfused-then-gated, lean vs tcgen05) that used the same transplanted number. `max|d|` stays printed beside the worst cell's fraction of the bound in every message, so a calibration or a regression is a number, never a silent widening.
* The **LSE keeps its 2e-2 bar**; the plant margins of the adversarial cell are untouched; **the oracle is unchanged**.
* `qkvg_from_hf`'s docstring gains the measured consequence of its documented bf16 `(1 + w)` rounding; the docs sentence on the lean / tcgen05 agreement names the bound.

## Why (the measurement behind it)

On the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next geometry (bf16, 24 / 2 heads, `d_head` 256, T 2048, B 1, the identity block list), the three FROST sparse arms read **max|d| = 0.0215 on exactly one gated-O element in 12,582,912** against the fp32 oracle -- row 5 (six visible keys), one head, one near-cancelling dim (two dominant keys with large opposite-sign V) -- and were refused by the 2e-2 bar.

Three independent re-derivations from the kernel's dumped operands reproduce the value bitwise on all 256 dims of that row: the mechanism is the **documented** bf16 rounding of the QK-RMSNorm weight `(1 + w)` in `qkvg_from_hf` (fp32 `(1 + w)` rounded once into the activation dtype; `norm_weight_offset` 0), which flips ~30 % of the normed `q` and ~27 % of the `k` elements by one bf16 ulp against the fp32-`(1 + w)` reference (an HF-faithful chain shows ~7 % from its own rope-dim rounding) and shifts that row's softmax weights by up to 1.5 %. Under the block's own operand convention the sparse core sits at the bf16-P floor (one ulp); the element is a property of the operand convention, not of any kernel. Rows attending >= 1024 keys stay within ~2e-3, which is why the decode suites (every row >= 2048 keys; ~1,460 gate records, worst 0.0020) never showed it.

Under the output bound the same tensors read **0.877 of the bound** (cos 0.99999; 0 elements above it) for the FROST sparse arms, 0.717 for the dense FROST route and 0.331 for the vLLM reference arm -- recorded, not hidden. The fp32 in-kernel offset form (`norm_weight_offset = 1.0`, HF-faithful numerics) stays a separate, later lever.

**Tolerances:** the oracle is unchanged; the bound is the repo's existing output convention (calibrated once on Rubin cc 10.7 for the block backward: accept cells at 0.40-0.66 of it). Nothing is widened for the LSE or for `out`.

## RED -> GREEN

On the real dumped tensors of that cell (CPU): the old assertion refuses the FROST sparse arms (`gated O off the oracle by 0.021484375 (budget 0.02)`); `assert_output_close` passes them at 0.8767 of the bound (`n_above_bound 0`, `cos 0.999989`); the dense route (0.7173) and the vLLM arm (0.3307) pass under both. The helper refuses a planted one-element excursion (44x the bound) and accepts a pure bf16 rounding of the reference (0.14).

## Tests

Host tier (A100 host; the Rubin cells skip): `test_block_qsa_decode.py` 30 passed / 90 skipped, `test_block_qsa_end_to_end.py` 3 passed / 99 skipped, `test_block_backward.py` 40 passed / 70 skipped (combined 73 / 259 / 0 failed).

Rubin cc 10.7 (shared development GPU, functional only): `test_block_qsa_decode.py` **120 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped** (349 s) and `test_block_qsa_end_to_end.py` **102 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped** (344 s), the whole L0 modules, one process each on a shared cc 10.7 GPU. Across the 359 gated-O comparisons the new helper printed, the worst cell sits at **0.544 of the bound** (decode) / **0.541** (end-to-end), no element above it, the gated-O cosine >= 0.999990. The backward module imports the shared constants and collects unchanged (its host cells pass; its Rubin gradient cells are not re-run here -- the constants are the same numbers).

`black -l 160` + `pre-commit` (black, SPDX) pass on the six files.

## Sibling suites (not changed here)

`test_block_qsa_fp8_kv.py` and `test_block_serving_extend.py` carry their own `2e-2` on the gated O; their cells attend long histories and are not exposed. Moving them to the shared helper is a follow-up.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""The OUTPUT tolerance convention of the gated attention block's suites -- ONE definition, shared by the forward suites
+(``test_block_qsa_end_to_end.py``, ``test_block_qsa_decode.py``) and the backward suite (``test_block_backward.py``).
+
+A bf16 / f16 output of the block is held to its fp32 / fp64 oracle PER ELEMENT at
+
+    |got - ref| <= atol_frac * max|ref| + rtol * |ref|        and        cos(got, ref) >= 0.999
+
+with ``rtol = 2^-6`` / ``atol_frac = 2^-7`` for bf16 and ``2^-9`` / ``2^-10`` for f16 (three more mantissa bits at every rounding
+point).  CALIBRATED ONCE from the first two full Rubin runs of the block backward (cc 10.7, 212 SMs; accept cells at 0.40-0.66 of
+the bound, identical numbers on both runs) and never widened; every assertion prints the worst cell as a FRACTION of the bound
+(``bound_ratio``) beside ``max|d|``, so a calibration or a regression is a number, never a silent widening.
+
+Why a tensor-scaled per-element bound and not one absolute ``atol`` on the gated O: an absolute ``2e-2`` was the SDPA stage test's
+bar on the LSE (``test_sdpa_stage_sm107.py``; its O checks are ``cos > 0.999``), transplanted onto bf16 O values of magnitude up to
+~3, where ONE bf16 ulp is 0.015625 (78 % of it) and any single rounding flip at ``|O| >= 4`` (ulp 0.03125) would exceed it for every
+implementation alike.  Measured on the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next geometry (bf16, 24 / 2 heads, d 256, T 2048; 2026-10-28): the block's
+documented bf16 ``(1 + w)`` QK-norm weight rounding (``qkvg_from_hf``) moves a SHORT row's gated O (6 visible keys; two dominant keys
+with large opposite-sign V at one dim) by 0.0215 against the fp32-``(1 + w)`` oracle -- one element in 12.6 M, 0.877 of this bound,
+cos 0.999989 -- while every row with >= 1024 keys stays within ~2e-3.  The oracle is unchanged by this convention.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+
+OUTPUT_RTOL = {torch.bfloat16: 2.0**-6, torch.float16: 2.0**-9}
+OUTPUT_ATOL_FRAC = {torch.bfloat16: 2.0**-7, torch.float16: 2.0**-10}
+OUTPUT_COS_MIN = 0.999
+_CHUNK = 1 << 26  # elements per fp64 reduction chunk of the cosine (a 2 GB fp64 copy of a 32k-token O never materializes)
+
+
+def cos64(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    """The cosine in fp64 accumulation, chunked (an fp32 dot over 10^7+ elements drifts past 1.0; the GPU lanes measured 1.003 once)."""
+    a, b = a.detach().reshape(-1), b.detach().reshape(-1)
+    if a.numel() == 0:
+        return 1.0
+    dot = na = nb = 0.0
+    for lo in range(0, a.numel(), _CHUNK):
+        x, y = a[lo : lo + _CHUNK].double(), b[lo : lo + _CHUNK].double()
+        dot += float(x @ y)
+        na += float(x @ x)
+        nb += float(y @ y)
+    if na == 0.0 and nb == 0.0:
+        return 1.0  # two all-zero tensors (every row dead) agree exactly
+    denom = math.sqrt(na) * math.sqrt(nb)
+    return dot / denom if denom > 0 else float("nan")
+
+
+def _bound_terms(got: torch.Tensor, rtol: Optional[float], atol_frac: Optional[float]) -> tuple:
+    if rtol is None:
+        if got.dtype not in OUTPUT_RTOL:
+            raise ValueError(f"no output bound is defined for {got.dtype}; pass rtol / atol_frac explicitly")
+        rtol = OUTPUT_RTOL[got.dtype]
+    if atol_frac is None:
+        if got.dtype not in OUTPUT_ATOL_FRAC:
+            raise ValueError(f"no output bound is defined for {got.dtype}; pass rtol / atol_frac explicitly")
+        atol_frac = OUTPUT_ATOL_FRAC[got.dtype]
+    return float(rtol), float(atol_frac)
+
+
+def output_bound_stats(got: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor, *, rtol: Optional[float] = None, atol_frac: Optional[float] = None) -> dict:
+    """The statistics of ``got`` against ``ref`` under the output bound (the dtype of ``got`` picks ``rtol`` / ``atol_frac`` unless given):
+    ``max_abs`` (max |d|, the recorded statistic), ``max_ref`` (max |ref|), ``bound_ratio`` (the worst element's |d| as a fraction of its
+    bound; <= 1 means within), ``n_above_bound``, ``cos`` (fp64), ``finite``, the ``worst`` element's index / values, and the bound's terms.
+    Both tensors are compared where they live (fp32 arithmetic on their device; the cosine in fp64)."""
+    rtol, atol_frac = _bound_terms(got, rtol, atol_frac)
+    got32, ref32 = got.detach().float(), ref.detach().float()
+    if got32.shape != ref32.shape:
+        raise ValueError(f"shape mismatch: got {tuple(got32.shape)} vs ref {tuple(ref32.shape)}")
+    finite = bool(torch.isfinite(got32).all())
+    if got32.numel() == 0:
+        return dict(max_abs=0.0, max_ref=0.0, bound_ratio=0.0, n_above_bound=0, cos=1.0, finite=True, rtol=rtol, atol_frac=atol_frac, worst=None, n_elements=0)
+    ref_max = float(ref32.abs().max())
+    diff = (got32 - ref32).abs()
+    bound = atol_frac * ref_max + rtol * ref32.abs()
+    if ref_max > 0:
+        ratio = diff / bound
+        i = int(torch.argmax(ratio.reshape(-1)))
+        bound_ratio = float(ratio.reshape(-1)[i])
+    else:  # an all-zero reference: the bound is 0 everywhere, so any difference is outside it
+        i = int(torch.argmax(diff.reshape(-1)))
+        bound_ratio = 0.0 if float(diff.max()) == 0.0 else float("inf")
+    n_above = int((diff > bound).sum())
+    idx = [int(x) for x in torch.unravel_index(torch.tensor(i), diff.shape)]
+    return dict(
+        max_abs=float(diff.max()),
+        max_ref=ref_max,
+        bound_ratio=bound_ratio,
+        n_above_bound=n_above,
+        cos=cos64(got32, ref32),
+        finite=finite,
+        rtol=rtol,
+        atol_frac=atol_frac,
+        n_elements=int(diff.numel()),
+        worst=dict(
+            index=idx, got=float(got32.reshape(-1)[i]), ref=float(ref32.reshape(-1)[i]), abs_diff=float(diff.reshape(-1)[i]), bound=float(bound.reshape(-1)[i])
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def format_output_stats(what: str, s: dict, *, cos_min: float = OUTPUT_COS_MIN) -> str:
+    return (
+        f"{what}: max|d|={s['max_abs']:.4g} max|ref|={s['max_ref']:.4g} worst cell {s['bound_ratio']:.3f} of the bound "
+        f"(rtol={s['rtol']}, atol={s['atol_frac']}*max|ref|; {s['n_above_bound']} of {s['n_elements']} elements above it) cos={s['cos']:.6f} (floor {cos_min})"
+        + (f" at {s['worst']['index']}: got {s['worst']['got']:.6g} ref {s['worst']['ref']:.6g}" if s.get("worst") else "")
+    )
+
+
+def assert_output_close(
+    got: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor, what: str, *, rtol: Optional[float] = None, atol_frac: Optional[float] = None, cos_min: float = OUTPUT_COS_MIN
+) -> dict:
+    """The output bound as an assertion: finite, ``cos >= cos_min``, no element above ``atol_frac * max|ref| + rtol * |ref|``.  Prints the
+    magnitudes (``max|d|`` kept as the recorded statistic beside the fraction of the bound) and returns ``output_bound_stats``."""
+    s = output_bound_stats(got, ref, rtol=rtol, atol_frac=atol_frac)
+    msg = format_output_stats(what, s, cos_min=cos_min)
+    print(msg)
+    assert s["finite"], f"{what}: non-finite cells"
+    assert s["cos"] >= cos_min, msg
+    assert s["n_above_bound"] == 0 and s["bound_ratio"] <= 1.0, msg
+    return s
